title: Implement the committed-schema generator stamp: export writes it, check gains the unattributable outcome
description:
Implements the mechanism specified in docs/specs/committed-schema-generator-stamp.md (LCLI-563), which is the spec half of OPAG-354 item 3. Split out because the five deliverables -- spec, export writing the stamp, check's third outcome and its exit code, the post-change churn re-measurement, and the rollout note -- do not fit one pull request under the SDLC size ceiling. Split endorsed by opum-agent 2026-09-20. The architectural commitment is OPAG-354's and is not reopened here; the mechanism is settled in the spec and is not reopened either.

READ THE SPEC FIRST. It carries the decision table, the refutation of the set-containment refinement, and the reason a version string is not committed. The two things most likely to be got wrong without it:

1. THE DIGEST IS THE DECISION KEY AND NO VERSION IS COMMITTED. schemaDriftFindings compares committed against regenerated bytes with a plain inequality (src/core/check.ts:794-829), so a committed version field is rewritten by every release in every repository whether or not the profile changed -- 21 informationless rewrites across v0.6.1/v0.6.2/v0.7.0 on this repository's own measured history. The running binary supplies its own version for the message. Ruling by opum-agent, 2026-09-20.

2. PRUNE IS ADVISED ONLY WHEN THE BINARY CAN AFFIRM IT OWNS THE ARTIFACT. Orphan plus a matching stamp digest is a real finding; orphan plus a differing stamp, and orphan plus NO stamp, are both the third outcome and never a prune. The no-stamp case is the COMMON case on the release that introduces this -- all 71 committed schemas fleet-wide are unstamped today -- so it is the default path, not an edge case.

WHERE THE CODE IS. Emission is emitSchemaFiles (src/core/schema.ts:676-694), which is the single source lore init and lore schema export share, so a scaffolded file and a re-exported one stay byte-identical -- the stamp has to land there, and it has to land on the alias files a renamed type emits (LCLI-553) or they report as drifted. The drift decision is schemaDriftFindings (src/core/check.ts:794-829), called via schemaDriftForRoot from src/commands/check.ts:239.

THE ASYMMETRY IS A REQUIREMENT, NOT A STYLE NOTE (OPAG-354 item 5). "No longer matches what this profile generates" rewrites a file and git recovers it; "no type owns this schema -- prune it" deletes one. They must not converge on one message or one exit code as the implementation grows.

TESTING THIS NEEDS THE PAIR, NOT THE PASS. The gate must be shown to REJECT (an orphan with an unrecognised stamp does not advise a prune, and exits distinguishably) and to ACCEPT (a clean stamped bundle exits 0), as two separate measurements, with the other checks green on both. A suite that only proves the new outcome fires cannot tell a working gate from one that is always in the third state -- which is the failure mode this whole mechanism is about, one level up.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore schema export writes x-lore-generator.profileDigest into every emitted file, including the byte-identical alias files a renamed type emits (LCLI-553)
lore check keys its prune/no-prune decision on the stamp rather than on type ownership alone

An orphaned schema whose stamp the running binary does not recognise -- INCLUDING one carrying no stamp at all -- produces a third outcome distinguishable in the exit code from both clean and drifted, and NEVER suggests pruning

The rewrite case and the delete case stay distinguishable in message and in schemaClass; the exit code separates an affirmed delete from an unaffirmed one (6 vs 7). Amended 2026-09-22 per opum-agent ruling on OPAG-354 (option A): the original "in both message and exit code" was a looser restatement of OPAG-354 item 5, which places the separation in a third outcome, and contradicted the spec decision table (stale and affirmed-orphaned both exit 6).
The exit code chosen for the third outcome is reconciled with the documented set in ADR-0005 (0/2/3/4/5/6), and the CLI-contract change is recorded rather than assumed
The gate is proven to REJECT and to ACCEPT as two separate measurements, with the other checks green on both commits
The churn cost is re-measured against this repository tags AFTER the change and stated, so the objection is closed with a number rather than a judgement
A rollout note ships with the release that introduces it, since all 71 committed schemas fleet-wide go unattributable at once -- LCLI-545 records what that felt like at 0.8.0

implementationNotes:
HANDOFF NOTE, session recycled at context budget 2026-09-21. Written here rather than left to the flush because the flush writes NO tracker note in this state and that silence is indistinguishable from a successful write: it requires EXACTLY ONE task In Progress (there are zero, verified by `quest task list --status "In Progress" --json`) and it skips the note on a clean, fully-pushed tree by design (OMARK-23). Two of its three silent conditions hold at once. The cursor at .claude/handovers/cursor.md is restart acceleration only and is outranked by this record and by live git.

STATE AT HANDOFF, verified from refs rather than remembered. origin/dev == origin/main == 2e5e736d543746896884672860eaabe31a250d8f. Zero open PRs (`gh pr list --state open`). Clean working tree, local branches down to dev and main. LCLI-561, LCLI-563 and LCLI-564 are Done and promoted; this task (LCLI-565) is To Do and deliberately UNOPENED -- that was chosen as the handoff seam because everything needed to start it is written down rather than held in a session's head.

START HERE. Read docs/specs/committed-schema-generator-stamp.md first, then this task's own description, which names the two things most likely to be got wrong without the spec. Do not re-derive the mechanism: it is settled, and the churn measurement that settles it is in the spec as a table. The architectural commitment is OPAG-354's and is not reopened; the mechanism was delegated here and is now decided.

THE ONE DECISION STILL OPEN inside LCLI-565 is which exit code the third outcome takes. lore's documented set (0 ok, 2 usage, 3 not_found, 4 denied, 5 conflict, 6 validation/drift) has no spare slot with the right meaning, so adding one is an ADR-0005 CLI-contract change. It is AC[5] on this task rather than prose in the spec. That is a design question by the fleet's own two-question test (it changes an external contract), so route it to opum-agent before implementing rather than deciding it locally -- the rest of the task is implementation and is yours.

WHAT THE REST OF THE BOARD LOOKS LIKE. LCLI-560 (retire the snapshot-retention spec) and LCLI-562 (release the epic) are both blocked behind LCLI-548 and the rest of the LCLI-546 epic, all still To Do -- do not start either. LCLI-546 itself is To Do and carries two correction notes worth reading if anything touches the opum-workflow sync hook. LCLI-482 (npm trusted publishing broken) is still open and is why any release ships without provenance; LCLI-544's lockfile constraint fires at the next version bump.

FOUR THINGS ESTABLISHED THIS SESSION THAT ARE NOT DERIVABLE FROM THE DIFF, and each cost a wrong belief first:

1. A CI re-run does NOT destroy the failing job log. Each attempt gets its own job id and keeps its log indefinitely; run 35545097732's attempt-1 windows job 106169476606 still served 642362 bytes hours later. `gh api .../jobs/<id>/logs` needs --allow-escape-sequences or it writes ZERO BYTES and exits 1, which reads exactly like the log being gone. Run ARTIFACTS are what a re-run genuinely replaces (LCLI-531, docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md); generalising that true artifact finding to logs is what produced the wrong rule. ci.yml's triage block now carries both commands. Routed fleet-wide as opum-agent OPAG-367, where re-measurement before landing is AC1 -- my numbers are relayed there, not reproduced.

2. Verify an installed fix by grepping the DIRECTORY for a unique symbol, not one expected file for a command literal. opum-workflow 0.10.2 split detection into hooks/_lib.sh (opum_deleted_tracked_files / opum_new_deletions) and left only the remedy string, inside a printf'd message body, in the hook. Score a known-pre-fix version in the SAME invocation as a positive control, or an all-zero read is indistinguishable from an unfixed build.

3. An acceptance criterion can name a configuration that CANNOT OCCUR. LCLI-561's AC[5] asked for "one committed file between them" when the snapshot store is .lore/cache/snapshots/1 and .gitignore:50 ignores .lore/cache/ -- `git check-ignore -v` settles it in one line. Amended with the measurement rather than satisfied against a weaker reading. Consequence worth not losing: the published 0.8.0 blast radius is NARROWER than the records implied, and does not travel through a consumer's repository.

4. LCLI-564's fix is proven at the root cause and NOT proven at the symptom. The recovered log shows every assertion passing and rmSync throwing EBUSY in the finally; the retry path is covered by an injected-error unit test needing no Windows; the prefix contract reddens exactly 1 of 15 under mutation. But the windows job passed intermittently BEFORE the fix too, so the two green runs since are consistent with the fix rather than proof the flake is eliminated. If it recurs, the log is now recoverable -- do not re-run and assume the evidence is gone.

PROCESS NOTE FOR WHOEVER SWEEPS THIS REPO. opum-agent's fleet sweep read this session's WORKING TREE rather than a ref and reported a false positive (a task In Progress with all criteria checked, which neither origin/dev nor the PR head ever held). Filed as evidence on their OPAG-156. A ref read has no mid-transaction window; a working-tree read always does. If a sweep line about lore-cli looks wrong, check which of the two it did before acting on it.

SKILLS THE NEXT SESSION SHOULD REACH FOR: opum-sdlc before any branch or PR, opum-lore's `lore` skill for anything under docs/ (and gate with `bun run lore check`, from source as CI does -- the PATH binary is older than this tree and its `schema export` advice REVERTS unreleased schema work), and opum-quest for tracker writes. This repository gates dev, not main: rules/branches/main returns []. Promotion is ordinary delivery and needs no grant.

Started 2026-09-22 after opum-doc ADR (require-generator-provenance-...-third-lore-check-outcome, origin/dev 645071a, ODOC-259) ruled exit 7 for the third outcome. error_type chosen: indeterminate. Argued to opum-agent: (1) 6+7 precedence in one run is undecided -- implementing 7-over-6 provisionally; (2) the only schema delete in source is lore schema export's pruneOrphans (src/commands/schema.ts:212-235), not lore sync, so the guard must live in export.

Implementation finding for AC[7]'s rollout note: an UNSTAMPED schema whose type still exists reports STALE (exit 6), not unattributable, and one lore schema export re-stamps it. Only unstamped ORPHANS go to exit 7. So the first stamping release moves every committed schema to exit 6, not 7 -- AC[7]'s 'go unattributable at once' is the wrong outcome name. AC[3] conflicts with the spec's table (stale and affirmed-orphaned both exit 6); ruling requested from opum-agent 2026-09-22.

AC[0]-AC[5] checked 2026-09-22 against PR opum-ai/lore-cli#224. REJECT: head 1289fb3b (probe: unstamped orphan .lore/schemas/probe-orphan.schema.json), run 35787089985 -- lore check (docs gate) failed with exit code 7 and [schema-unattributable], every other job green incl. docker e2e. ACCEPT: head 124832f3 (probe reverted), run 35787585093 -- all 12 executed jobs green, docs gate exit 0. Decision-table rows observed on a compiled binary (clean 0 / missing 6 / stale 6 rewrite msg / matching-stamp orphan 6 prune msg / foreign or no stamp 7 never-prune / mixed 7 with every schemaClass in --json). AC[4]: dated ADR-0005 amendment + cli-contract.md 5.5, manifest taxonomy 9 keys. Two adversarial reviewer passes; every finding fixed with a test shown red without its fix (incl. a pre-existing APFS case-variant prune that deleted an unstamped ADR.schema.json on the old build). OPEN: AC[6] churn re-measurement, AC[7] rollout note -- task stays In Progress. Outside the fleet: ECK-ALIGNMENT.md D3 records ECK adopting exit codes 0/2/3/4/5/6 verbatim; left as dated history, ECK side to be told via the user.

ROLLOUT REQUIREMENT for AC[7] (opum-agent ruling on OPAG-326, opum-ai/opum-agent#887, 2026-09-22): no fleet repository bumps its docs lore pin to 0.8.0; each moves straight to the FIRST release carrying LCLI-565, and its lore schema export re-stamp lands in the SAME pull request as the pin change (the release makes every committed schema STALE, so a pin-only PR goes red). The rollout note must tell consumers exactly that: pin + export in one PR. opum-agent briefs repositories one at a time once lore-cli names the release. Also: opum-doc ADR (main fc43bfc) never claimed committed-profile repos are always attributable, so the spec correction needs no ADR amendment; the APFS case-variant deletion path is recorded on OPAG-326 as NOT shown to be LCLI-546's mechanism.

AC[6] re-measured 2026-09-22 AFTER the change. Method: git archive of src/ at v0.6.0, v0.6.1, v0.6.2, v0.7.0, v0.8.0 and HEAD; each tag's compile patched to expose requiredFields with the identical derivation (fieldOrder.filter(f => merged[f]?.required === true)); the new profileDigest projection computed over each tag's built-in profile (loadProfile on an empty dir) plus a per-type hash of jsonSchema. POSITIVE CONTROL: the script's HEAD digest sha256:a6d120fa...72005 equals the stamp committed in origin/dev .lore/schemas/epic.schema.json byte for byte. Result per transition (stamp-only rewrite = digest moved while that file's body did not): v0.6.0->v0.6.1 digest same, 0; v0.6.1->v0.6.2 same, 0; v0.6.2->v0.7.0 digest CHANGED but all 7 bodies changed too, 0; v0.7.0->v0.8.0 same, 0; v0.8.0->dev digest CHANGED (Arc type added, a genuine type-set change the digest exists to see), 6 of 8 re-stamped with unchanged bodies. Over v0.6.1/v0.6.2/v0.7.0, where a committed version field measured 21 informationless rewrites, the digest produces 0. One-time cost separate from this: the first stamping release rewrites every committed schema once (unstamped -> stamped). Also confirmed by the 0.9.0 bump (LCLI-566): bumping the version moved no committed schema byte.
finalSummary: Delivered across PR opum-ai/lore-cli#224 (implementation), #225 (OPAG-326 rollout ruling), #227 (0.9.0 bump + CHANGELOG rollout note), #228 promotion, and published as @opum-ai/lore 0.9.0 on 2026-09-22 (tag v0.9.0 -> 48840cb3 -> fd712748; Release run 35794336818). AC[0]-[5] evidenced by #224's REJECT run 35787089985 (docs gate exit 7 on an unstamped probe orphan, all other jobs green) and ACCEPT run 35787585093 (all green). AC[3] amended per opum-agent's OPAG-354 ruling (message + schemaClass distinguish rewrite vs delete; exit code separates affirmed 6 from unaffirmed 7). AC[6]: churn re-measured post-change, 0 informationless rewrites over v0.6.1/v0.6.2/v0.7.0 vs 21 for a committed version field, positive control matching the committed stamp. AC[7]: rollout note shipped in CHANGELOG [0.9.0] and the GitHub Release; verified on the PUBLISHED binary that lore check exits 7 on an unstamped orphan and the manifest carries indeterminate:7. Downstream told: opum-agent, opum-marketplace (skills/ tree 38683e10), opum-cli-e2e, quest-cli. Open elsewhere: LCLI-546 mechanism unresolved; ECK-ALIGNMENT D3 exit-code note is the user's to send.
